pillars.title: Nouns, Definiteness (الْـ), Tanween & Gender
pillars.summary: Definite الْـ (Ma'rifah) vs. proper names without الْـ (U1L1); dropping الْـ for indefinite Tanween ـٌ (Nakirah) and equational predicates (U1L13–U1L14); feminine Taa Marbootah ة/ـة nouns (U1L2–U1L5), feminine adjective conversion (Stage 3 p. 76), feminine demonstratives (U1L17), feminine pronouns (U4L9–U4L12), and 3rd-singular feminine past verb agreement (U7L7).

pillars.title: Number Systems (Singular, Dual / Tasniyah, Sound & Broken Plurals)
pillars.summary: Singular noun base (U1L1–U1L9); Broken Plurals (Jama Mukassar, U1L10 & U5L4) and Sound Feminine Plurals (ـَاتٌ, U1L11); Dual / Tasniyah (ـَانِ / ـَيْنِ, U3L10); Sound Masculine Plurals (ـُونَ / ـِينَ, U5L1–U5L3); plural detached/attached pronouns & demonstratives (U5L5–U5L18); plural present, prohibitive, passive, and past verb forms.

pillars.title: Case Endings (Raf', Nasb, Jarr) & Case Triggers
pillars.summary: Raf' (ـُ / ـٌ / ـَانِ / ـُونَ) on baseline nouns and verbal subjects (Faa'il, U6L3); Jarr (ـِ / ـٍ / ـَيْنِ / ـِينَ) triggered by prepositions (U2L2–U2L7, U5L23), oath وَ (U2L10), and Mudaaf Ilaih (U3L4–U3L7); Nasb (ـَ / ـًا / ـَيْنِ / ـِينَ) triggered by إِنَّ/أَنَّ, لَا, إِلَّا, كَانَ, Haal (U4L17), Tamyeez (U5L22), and Maf'ool (U6L3); plus verbal mood Nasb and Jazm.

pillars.title: Prepositions (Huroof-e-Jarr) & High-Frequency Particles
pillars.summary: Conjunction وَ (U1L12) and emphatic لَـ (U1L18); core prepositions (لِـ, فِي, عَلَىٰ, مِنْ, إِلَىٰ, بِـ) and particles (إِنَّ, لَا, إِلَّا, وَ, أَنَّ, يَا) in U2L1–U2L13; pronoun fusions in Units 4–5; restrictive & sentence-opening particles (U5L19–U5L20); verbal prefixes and past-verb connectors (فَـ, إِذْ, مَا, قَدْ, لَمَّا, إِذَا, لَوْ, لَوْلَا).
examples: لَنْ نَصْبِرَ ، أَنْ يَتُوبَ ، لِيَغْفِرَ ، لَمْ يَجْعَلْ
فَعَلِمَ ، قَدْ جَعَلْنَا ، لَوْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ

pillars.title: Pronouns (Detached & Attached — Singular, Dual/Plural)
pillars.summary: Singular detached & attached pronouns across 4 persons/genders: هُوَ/ـهُ (U4L1–U4L4), أَنْتَ/ـكَ (U4L5–U4L8), هِيَ/ـهَا (U4L9–U4L12), أَنَا/ـي/ـنِي (U4L13–U4L16); plural detached & attached pronouns: هُمْ/ـهُمْ (U5L5–U5L8), أَنْتُمْ/ـكُمْ (U5L9–U5L12), نَحْنُ/ـنَا (U5L13–U5L16); dual ـهُمَا in وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا (U5L21); and attached object pronouns on present & past verbs.
examples: أَنْتَ يُوسُفُ ، بَيْتُكَ ، هِيَ فِتْنَةٌ ، بَيْتُهَا

pillars.title: Nominal & Genitive Compounds (Tawseefi, Izaafi, Ishaari)
pillars.summary: Ishaari demonstratives هَٰذَا, ذَٰلِكَ, هٰذِهِ, تِلْكَ (U1L15–U1L17) and plural أُولٰئِكَ, هٰؤُلَاءِ (U5L17–U5L18); Tawseefi noun + adjective agreement (U3L1–U3L3, preceded by Stage 3 p. 76); Izaafi possessive chains (Mudaaf drops tanween, Mudaaf Ilaih takes Jarr, U3L4–U3L7, U5L3), including كُلُّ (U3L7) and noun + attached pronoun chains.
examples: هَٰذَا كِتَابٌ ، ذَٰلِكَ الْفَضْلُ ، أُولَٰئِكَ مُسْلِمُونَ
رَبُّ الْمَشْرِقِ ، كِتَابُ اللَّهِ ، فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ

pillars.title: Active & Passive Participles (Ism Faa'il, Ism Maf'ool, Ism Tafzeel)
pillars.summary: Ism-ut-Tafzeel (أَفْعَلُ, U1L19, paired with Tamyeez U5L22 and مِنْ comparison U7L1); triliteral Ism Faa'il (فَاعِلٌ) and intensive Mubalaghah (فَعَّالٌ, U3L8); derived active and passive participles with مُـ (U3L9); triliteral Ism Maf'ool (مَفْعُولٌ, U4L18); and sound masculine plural participles (U5L1–U5L2).

pillars.title: Verb System (Mudhari', Amr, Nahi, Shart, Nasb/Jazm, Majhool, Maazi)
pillars.summary: Proto-verbs كَانَ (U2L12), لَيْسَ (U5L20), Amr قُلْ (U5L21); complete Unit 6 Fe'l Mudhari' (3rd/2nd/1st persons, active & passive Majhool, Nahi, Shart, Nasb, Jazm); and complete Unit 7 single-sighah Fe'l Maazi mastery (عَمِلَ, عَبَدُوا, جَعَلْنَا, عَبَدْتُمْ, عَبَدْتُ, عَبَدْتَ, عَبَدَتْ, plus passive أُنْزِلَ and أُخْرِجُوا) including weak/irregular and derived stems.
examples: يَعْبُدُ ← تَعْبُدُ ، يَعْبُدُونَ ، تَعْبُدُونَ ، أَعْبُدُ ، نَعْبُدُ
لَا تَقْتُلُوا ، لَا تَظْلِمْ ، لَا تَدْعُ ، لَا تَخَفْ
مَنْ يَشْكُرْ ، أَنْ يَتُوبَ ، لِيَغْفِرَ ، لَمْ يَجْعَلْ

pillars.title: Recurring Qur'anic Idioms (Muhaawaraat)
pillars.summary: Idiomatic clause frames taught as whole semantic templates: restrictive negation (U5L19), 15 foundational idioms (U5L21), emphatic Min negation (U5L23), relative/conditional Mudhari' idioms (U6L4, U6L7, U6L11, U6L13, U6L16–U6L17, U6L19), past-verb Muhaawaraat anchored to خَلَقَ, قَالَ, كَانَ, كَفَرُوا, جَعَلْنَا, رَأَيْتُمْ, حَبِطَتْ, أُنْزِلَ, أُوتُوا (U7L1–U7L9), and 10 capstone rhetorical styles (U7L10).
examples: مَنْ يَشَاءُ ، أَفَلَا يَعْلَمُونَ ، مَنْ يَشْكُرْ
أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ ، قَالَ لِقَوْمِهِ ، كَانُوا يَكْسِبُونَ
لَوْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ ، أَفَمَنْ ... كَمَنْ ، إِنَّهُ لَا يُفْلِحُ الظَّالِمُونَ
